title: AI-Powered Tools for Enhancing Writing Skills of English Language Learners: A Systematic Literature Review
venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science (IJRISS)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the growing use of artificial intelligence tools to support English writing among English as a Second Language (ESL) and English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners. The review asks two main questions: which AI tools have been used to enhance writing skills, and how these tools improve different dimensions of writing. The authors argue that rapid AI development, especially since 2023, has outpaced earlier reviews and created a need for an updated synthesis.

Using PRISMA 2020 procedures, the authors systematically reviewed 31 studies published between 2021 and 2025 from ERIC and Web of Science. The included studies covered a range of methodologies and focused mainly on AI-powered writing tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, QuillBot, Gemini, and other automated writing evaluation or feedback systems. The synthesis examined outcomes across grammar and mechanics, vocabulary and style, feedback and revision, and narrative writing.

The reviewed evidence largely concerns student populations in ESL/EFL contexts, with a strong skew toward tertiary education and limited representation from primary and secondary settings. The paper notes that the included studies span varied sample sizes and designs, including mixed-methods, quasi-experimental, experimental, qualitative, and case studies. The review is not confined to one country; it synthesizes studies from multiple contexts, though a single study-country for the review itself is not specified beyond the authors’ institutional affiliation in Malaysia.

The main conclusion is that AI tools generally function as effective writing supports, especially for feedback and revision, grammar accuracy, and vocabulary development. ChatGPT was the most frequently studied tool, followed by Grammarly, QuillBot, and Gemini. The authors conclude that AI tools can improve ESL/EFL learners’ writing quality, but they also caution that AI should supplement rather than replace teachers, and that more longitudinal and non-tertiary research is needed to determine whether gains persist after the tools are removed.

finding.finding_summary: The review reports that ChatGPT was the most prevalent tool and was consistently described as improving overall writing quality through immediate support for idea organization, essay structuring, and personalized feedback.
The review states that ChatGPT helped diversify vocabulary and improve expressiveness and fluency by offering personalized vocabulary suggestions and alternative phrasing.

The review reports that ChatGPT played a major role in feedback and revision processes, with studies describing instant critiques, self-paced revision, and improved essay quality, participation, and motivation when AI-generated feedback was used.
